headline: eBay beat in Q4 with GMV up 8% FX-neutral and announced a $1.2bn deal for Depop.
guidance_note: FY26 (ex-Depop): FX-neutral GMV growth similar to 2025, non-GAAP op income +8-10%; Q1 GMV $21.5-21.9bn (+10-12%), EPS $1.53-1.59 above consensus.
key_messages: GMV $21.2bn, +10% reported / +8% FX-neutral; revenue +15% reported / +13% FX-neutral.
Focus-category GMV grew 16%+, led by collectibles, parts & accessories, luxury, refurbished, apparel and sneakers; international lagged the US.
Active buyers ~135M; >134M ex-Tise, up ~1% organically. ~16M enthusiasts spend >$3,300 a year each.
Agreed to buy Depop from Etsy for $1.2bn; dividend raised 7% to $0.31 and buyback authorization raised by $2bn.

consumer.big_ticket: Holiday-quarter demand healthy in enthusiast and refurbished categories; international weaker than US.

macro_read: Holiday 2025 discretionary demand held up on eBay, with refurbished goods and collectibles growing and the US outperforming abroad. Buyer counts were nearly flat.
notes: Revenue $2.97bn comes from Zacks/Investing coverage; the release headline rounds it to $3.0bn.
Revenue consensus left null because sources disagree ($2.87bn vs $2.89bn). EPS consensus uses Zacks ($1.36); other outlets cited $1.35.
Stock reaction left null: shares rose ~6.8-7.3% after hours and ~7-8% premarket, but the Feb 19 close was not confirmed.
A call summary says return/cancellation rates stabilized as buyers and sellers adjusted to US trade-policy changes; the source text was truncated, so this is unconfirmed.
Tise acquisition adds ~1M buyers to the count.
